items.title: Using smart glasses technology to support the advanced skills competency of tissue viability nurses
items.summary: COVID-19 accelerated the use of technology in health care and forced health professionals to re-evaluate their approach to adopting new methods of healthcare delivery. In-person clinical supervision for new skill acquisition was often the only option before the COVID-19 pandemic.

items.title: Strategy to achieve hospital-acquired pressure ulcer improvement and an effective incident learning response
items.summary: Background: Preventing hospital-acquired pressure ulcers (HAPUs) remains a high priority safety concern on local and national agendas. Rigorous action plans and improvement strategies are central to reducing the incidence of PUs, which are largely preventable.

items.title: Impact of structured patient education on leg ulcer recurrence prevention following healing: results after one year
items.summary: Background: Venous leg ulcers (VLUs) are chronic, recurrent wounds associated with significant physical, psychological and healthcare burden. Despite effective healing rates with compression therapy, recurrence rates remain high, often exceeding 60% within 1 to 2 years.

items.summary: Non-healing wounds place a real and growing demand on healthcare services and on the people living with them (Stephen-Haynes and Toner, 2025; Mitchell, 2025).

items.title: Negative pressure wound therapy: Patient safety and risk management
items.summary: Negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) is an established intervention used across a range of clinical settings, from hospital-based acute and surgical care to community and home environments.

Welcome to the annual conference edition of Wounds UK
items.summary: As we get ready for Harrogate this year, I always like to give a quick overview of what’s coming up. The conference may feel a little different this year, as building works at the venue mean we’ll be in a different part of the building. No more trekking up the big, winding staircase.

items.title: The Wound Care Academy: A year of learning, collaboration and growth
items.summary: This joint Editorial focuses on the development and success of the Wound Care Academy (WCA), which was developed by Wounds UK as an innovative educational initiative designed to support the continuing professional development of healthcare professionals involved in wound prevention and management.

items.title: The Four Nations Stop the Pressure Campaign
items.summary: This year International Stop the Pressure Day falls on Thursday 19th November, but as always, our campaign activity will span the whole week hoping to raise the profile of pressure ulcer (PU) prevention for clinicians and the general public.

items.title: Wound care transformation needs more than evidence: It needs strategic leadership
items.summary: The evidence for improving wound care has never been stronger, yet variation in practice, delayed healing, patient harm and unwarranted costs remain common across the NHS.

items.title: Top ten tips: Skin assessment
items.summary: Within healthcare, skin assessment is a key component of nursing care, often recognised as a fundamental skill. It is nevertheless often carried out irregularly and in an unstructured way.

items.title: Impact pressure redistribution mattresses have on bed mobility and independence
items.summary: “A pressure ulcer (PU) is localised damage to the skin and/or underlying tissue…resulting from prolonged pressure or pressure in combination with shear” (NPIAP, EPUAP & PPPIA, 2025). They are painful and debilitating, impacting physical, social and psychological wellbeing along with length of stay.

items.title: Early reduced compression for lower-limb wounds: An acute care approach
items.summary: Chronic wounds, including leg ulcers, represent a significant burden to both patients and the NHS (Guest et al, 2015; National Wound Care Strategy Programme [NWCSP], 2020).

items.title: Bridging clinical expertise and project delivery: Collaborative success in implementing a digital wound app across community services
items.summary: Across community services, the pressure to deliver safe, consistent and effective wound care has never been greater. Rising caseloads, complex wounds and variation in documentation have created a clear need for digital solutions that support clinicians in real time.

items.title: Local infection management in pressure ulcers
items.summary: The incidence of pressure ulcers (PUs) is increasing worldwide, driven by an ageing population and the rising prevalence of chronic, multi-system disorders, such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease (Hajhosseini et al, 2020).

items.title: Lipoedema management with compression therapy
items.summary: Lipoedema is a progressive and incurable disorder that predominantly affects females and is associated with oestrogen and other hormonal changes (National Library of Medicine [NLM], 2023).

items.title: Evaluating malodour management using a cinnamon-based odour control dressing
items.summary: Malignant wounds can have a devastating impact on patients and their relatives, causing considerable physical and psychological distress. This distress can be overwhelming and significantly affect an individual’s overall quality of life (QoL; White and Kondasinghe, 2022).

items.title: Evidence-based practice: Role of service evaluation in wound care
items.summary: Service evaluation has become an integral part of contemporary healthcare practice, yet it remains variably understood and inconsistently applied.

items.title: Developing a formulary to standardise practice
items.summary: The NHS Plan (2025) places a clear emphasis on delivering consistent, evidence-based and cost-effective care, with a particular focus on reducing unwarranted variation and improving patient outcomes.

items.title: Removing the barriers and reclaiming ourselves
items.summary: In my last article (Molyneux, 2026a), I explored the hidden quest of authenticity. Not only its importance to our wellbeing and mental health, but more so, the ease of denial and distortion of our internal processes and selves. I also explored how we will often be unaware that we are doing this.

items.title: Vascular reform is on the agenda. Now we need action
items.summary: It was encouraging to be in Westminster Hall this month to hear MPs debating the need for reform of vascular care. For those of us who have spent years calling for better care for people with lower-limb conditions, the fact that vascular disease was being discussed in Parliament at all, felt significant.

items.title: Lindsay Leg Clubs: People and communities at winter time: A Leg Club philosophy
items.summary: As the autumn welcomes another turn of the season, we often find a brief time to reflect on the year to date and the months ahead. The winter period can be a challenging time for people at any age across the country as the days grow shorter and the evenings darker.

items.title: NHS Supply Chain's £113m Negative Pressure Wound Therapy framework names six suppliers
items.summary: NHS Supply Chain has signed six suppliers to its new Negative Pressure Wound Therapy (NPWT) framework, worth an estimated £113m over its four-year term to March 2031.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of pH 5.5 hypochlorous acid in the management of complex wounds in paediatric patients
items.summary: This case series describes the benefits of using of a non-cytotoxic acidic pH cleansing solution in the treatment of complex wounds in paediatric patients, at two health centres in Santiago, Chile.

items.title: Evaluation of Triketra, a chitosan-based wound healing gel, on acute/ hard-to-heal wounds: a single cohort non-comparative clinical pilot study
items.summary: Objective: This study investigated the safety and real-world effectiveness of ChitoCare Medical Triketra (Primex ehf, Iceland), a chitosan-based wound healing gel on a variety of acute and hard-to-heal wounds.
